query: For bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified predictive approach make to overcome the limited accuracy of available analytical predictions and their usual restriction to perfect, defect-free crystals? Address the nearly 0–200 K regime and the 300–1200 K regime, for which measurements also exist on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen; explain why the approach should improve accuracy, predict its advantage over existing analytical approaches, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a held-out conductivity benchmark and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A data-driven model that explicitly includes 1 wt.% oxygen-induced defect scattering in bulk HfNbTaTiZr provides more accurate thermal conductivity predictions from nearly 0–200 K and 300–1200 K than existing analytical approaches, which assume perfect crystals.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen, with nominally similar microstructure across the measured temperature regimes.
generation.intervention: Train and apply a machine learning framework that incorporates both experimentally measured oxygen effects and ab initio/analytical data for realistic defect scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
generation.conditions: Measurements and predictions performed from 0–200 K and 300–1200 K on a specimen with 1 wt.% oxygen and corresponding nominally pure references.
generation.structural_mediator: Oxygen-induced point defects that scatter phonons and electrons, altering thermal transport behavior relative to an ideal crystal model.
generation.mechanism: By accounting for actual lattice disorder and oxygen content in a data-driven model, phonon and electron scattering processes are treated beyond the perfect-crystal assumption, improving predictive fidelity over purely analytical methods.
generation.predicted_outcome: An improvement in prediction accuracy over conventional analytical methods by more than the current 5–10% deviation often observed in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes, especially at low temperatures where defect scattering notably impacts transport.
generation.baseline: Standard continuum or ab initio-based predictive formulas that ignore dopant/defect effects and typically show larger discrepancies when compared to real oxygen-bearing samples.
generation.boundary: Applicability is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr alloys with ~1 wt.% oxygen and similar microstructures; extrapolation to substantially higher oxygen contents or drastically different compositional variants remains to be validated.
generation.uncertainty: The precise gain in accuracy (e.g., 5% vs. 10% improvement) may vary with microstructure differences, measurement uncertainties, and the availability of representative training data at each temperature segment.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a separate bulk HfNbTaTiZr sample with 1 wt.% O (not used in model training). Measure thermal conductivity via a standardized laser flash method at discrete points in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K ranges.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the model’s predicted conductivity deviates by more than 5% (beyond measurement error) from the newly measured data at any temperature in the specified ranges, the hypothesis that the data-driven approach significantly improves accuracy is falsified.

Each of these approaches has its own strengths and weaknesses. For example, ab initio and MD are very time-consuming and can hardly be used to predict structures of the alloys in a high-throughput manner. Phenomenological rules are based on empirical observations and are easy for calculations, but the accuracy of their predictions does not exceed 72% []. CALPHAD modeling can be quite throughput, however it requires significant computing resources. In addition, the accuracy of the CALPHAD predictions can be limited due to the absence of a reliable database for HEAs []. The machine learning approach is sensitive to the size and composition of a training dataset, but the prediction accuracy of this method can attain more than 90% []. There are 370 RCCAs data points from the DFT calculation. A total of 90% of data were utilized for training, and 10% were used to test and validate the results. The three ML models used in this work are random forest (RF) regressor, gradient boosting regressor (GBR), and XGBoost (XGB) through the Scikit-learn library [], which is also used for data preparation and model assessment. The RF model is an ensemble approach consisting of many decision trees to improve prediction accuracy and reduce overfitting by averaging the trees. The samples of the training dataset may reappear in the single tree due to sampling replacement, also known as bootstrapping. GBR and XGB are multi-purpose machine learning methods that can handle both classification and regression problems. The GBR is a type of ensemble model having an iterative collection of tree models, and it is capable of learning from the previous model’s mistakes. The XGBoost [] is a powerful machine learning method that makes a quick decision by implementing boosted decision trees efficiently and effectively. chosen.why: A multi-temperature data-driven model explicitly accounting for oxygen doping and real lattice defects fills the method gap of perfect-crystal analytical models and so should yield more accurate predictions. Prior ML models of similar compositionally complex alloys have successfully integrated defect states and temperature dependence to improve fidelity. If the new model’s predictions differ from future carefully controlled thermal conductivity measurements (held out from training) by more than a pre-agreed margin (e.g., 5% beyond experimental uncertainty), this discrepancy would falsify the hypothesis that the approach offers superior predictive power over existing analytical models.
